correctness.rationale: The proof covers all measurable positive-area subsets. An epsilon-enclosing-disk argument avoids any compactness assumption on the candidate set. Brunn-Minkowski proves the centered disk-intersection area bound for every disk center, and the exact square-disk area derivative reduces the global scalar minimum to the unique root alpha=cos(alpha). The proposed optimizer has exact circumradius because it contains an antipodal pair at distance twice the proposed radius.

value.rationale: The result exactly solves a named circumradius replacement of the Cheeger problem on the square, a canonical domain. It identifies a non-obvious optimizer with radius strictly between the inradius and circumradius, gives an exact fixed-point constant, and supplies a reusable Brunn-Minkowski centering reduction for centrally symmetric domains.
